findings.reason: the counts are load-bearing — the section asserts "the counts are sized for the partition's one-hour limit" off the three-cold figure, and the done-when requires "the median of every read it ran"; at the plan's own medians five cold runs per read per arm take the cold-read time from about 40 min to about 67 min, over `all_debug`'s 1:00:00 limit, so §6 must either set the cold count to five and drop the one-hour sizing claim (or split the run), or not fix a cold count at all.
findings.text: §6 fixes "three cold runs and five warm runs of each read" yet names `health-tool-latency/scripts/profile_reads.py`, whose `main` calls `timed(f"{which}-cold", fn)` then `timed(f"{which}-warm", fn)` in one process, so every invocation yields exactly one cold and one warm sample; five warm runs therefore require five invocations, which also yield five cold samples, so "three cold runs" cannot be produced, and running three invocations instead leaves the "five warm runs" unmet

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §6 fixes "three cold runs and five warm runs of each read" but the profiler it names emits exactly one cold and one warm timed read per invocation, so those counts are not producible.
